hypotheses: H1: Cross-system transfer is real for these compounds, so a second line chosen for maximal tissue/target contrast (e.g., PC3 or YAPC) will often yield one active and one inactive label, increasing usable pairs.

H2: Shared systematic response or vehicle-norm thresholding dominates, so activity labels are largely line-independent; second-line choice will rarely create discordant pairs, and many compounds will remain single-label.
evidence_gaps: No measured response data shown for any compound-line pair; only availability and first_line are given.
Tissue-specific target dependence is not established for BRD4, IL12A, DPP4, EGFR, or the other targets.
Activity is a vehicle-norm threshold in L1000, not viability; mechanism cannot be inferred from two labels.
Repurposing Hub/MAP annotations are weaker than measured responses and do not prove causal target engagement.
No information on whether the first A375 observation is active or inactive for each compound.
